newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ICICI cuts prime lending rates.
newsitem.headline: India's ICICI cuts prime lending rates.

text.p: The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Ltd (ICICI) is reducing its medium term and long-term prime lending rates by 50 basis points, a top bank official told Reuters on Monday.
The new rates take effect on July 1, 1997, Kalpana Morparia, ICICI's general manager, said.

"In keeping with the trend of overall reduction in interest rates as signalled by the one percentage point cut in the bank rate by the Reserve Bank of India, ICICI today decided to reduce its lending rates," the bank said in a statement.

"Consistent with its policy of passing on the benefits of lower cost of funds to its borrowers, the medium term prime rate (MTPR) stands reduced from 13.5 percent to 13.0 percent, while its long term prime rate (LTPR) stands reduced from 15.0 percent to 14.5 percent," it said.
The new rates are effective July 1.
ICICI had in April announced a two-tier prime lending rate structure to address the short-term needs of its clients separately from their long-term requirements.
ICICI is India's second-largest term lending bank.
